design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 1 (warranty_claims_and_transfers). Draw (draw_counts.py --task 1): prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[6,6] -> labor billing 6, prorated share acceptance 6.
WHY A GOOD TEST: the owner only asks to go ahead with the prorated glass replacement and accept her share. The share policy says the share is fixed only after the records carry a labor charge entry for every visit on the claim that the terms bill labor for; the measuring visit of 2026-09-26 (outside the 1-year labor term) has a trip entry but no labor entry. The agent must bill that labor (six factors: labor-hours method giving the method hours, unit-count minimum, lead-safe allowance, crew, Saturday rate, senior program) and then work out the share (build-class charge, triple-pane and grilles upgrades from change orders covering every opening, volume rate, CareLine parts discount, and the visit credit for accepting within 30 days of the decision), then hand the acceptance to the owner.
SCOPE: task 0 claimed the missed-visit fee, trip billing and transfer fee policies and tools; this task claims warranty_ext_visit_labor_billing and warranty_ext_prorated_share_acceptance with bill_visit_labor_b6354c72 and accept_prorated_glass_share_5fbbc0c6. Union = all five policies; scopes disjoint.
PROBLEM TREE: share (user, root) <-value_input- labor (agent). Sentence (affirmative): 'The owner's share of a prorated replacement is fixed only after the records carry a labor charge entry for every technician visit on the claim that the warranty terms bill labor for.' Only the labor policy writes labor_charge entries. False at the opening (rows c1/c2). Skipping the labor write gives a share of 675.92 instead of 110.67.
BASE-INVARIANT CARD: both writes are warranty_charge_assessed; the five governing base policies carry no gate on that event (policy_scope). Base facts that frame scope hold on the records: the claim was filed 2026-09-15, 7 days after discovery 2026-09-08 (Limited notice window 30 days); glass term 10 years in force at 8 full years; labor term 1 year ended 2019-06-19; decision approved_with_proration for 4 units.
BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD: registration WR-4072519, seal-failure claim (4 units). Credit includes only charges on this claim (trip 163.88 and the new labor 565.25); excluded: the 2022 shipping fee on the hardware claim and the CareLine plan's own charges. Change orders: triple pane and grilles cover all 10 openings; laminated covers only 2 (near-miss, no laminated add-on).
FACTOR CARD: see computations[].factor_trace and factor_sensitivity; every factor off its fall-through. Near-misses: 2.2 h on site (ignored: a measuring visit's method hours are the labor minimum); laminated on 2 openings; CareLine visits are not warranty charges.
SEED: every row read by a gold find; history consistent with the charter at its dates (seed_consistency, including the 163.88 trip computed by the trip billing policy). CareLine Plus rows follow the service charter (plan fee 189.00 per term, rescreen of 3 screens at 39.00 each plus the 69.00 trip on a plan-year-2 repair visit).
PERSONA: chatty retired teacher; volunteers the fogged windows, the visit, the approval notice and the wish to accept; identity, registration number, window count and CareLine membership only when asked; agrees passively to any billing the agent explains; accepts with the figures handed over; closes when told the share is recorded.
STANDARD SOLUTION: locate/verify -> registration, claims, activities, window contract and its transactions, factory order, install job and its activities, service plan and calls -> bill labor 565.25 (4.0 billable labor hours, 2026-09-26) -> hand over the acceptance: 4 units, share 110.67.
VERIFICATION: scratch evaluator on check_compute primitives reproduced 565.25, 110.67 (675.92 without labor) and every sensitivity figure; per-task gates recorded at final run.
ROUND 2 REWORK (policy-task audit 2026-10-13): SOURCE-TASK RED (billable_hours 1.5 vs 4.0) -> the labor rule now names the method's output 'method hours' and defines 'billable labor hours' once, as the method hours raised by the lead-safe allowance and multiplied by the labor crew rate, booked on the charge to one decimal place; the tool's billable_hours argument is described as 'the billable labor hours of the visit as the warranty labor terms define them'; gold 4.0 / 565.25 unchanged. F-G1 -> rules say rounded half up to the cent (a half cent goes to the higher cent) and every result computes true half up; values unchanged. T1-O1 -> the two change_order_fee rows of 2018-03-29 were removed: the three change-order lines share one date, form one change order under the window charter and fall within the 1100 series' free count of 1. T1-O2 (realism) kept as company schedules: the lead-safe allowance follows the claim component and the crew rate the installation method, because sash removal to reach the sealed units disturbs painted trim and trim-wrapped units are worked by two technicians whatever the visit's purpose.
ROUND 3 REWORK (render-source findings and policy re-audit revision 2 observations): F2 -> the proration ladder now reads 'once five (ten) full years have been reached', matching full_years >= 5 / >= 10; the full-year count is stated. F3 -> the share rule defines a CareLine plan as any plan other than the On-Call Service Account. R2-O1 -> the labor baseline now says the billable labor hours start from the method hours, so it no longer reads as an identity outside the default case. On this world (start 2018-06-20, 8 full years; CareLine Plus) 565.25 and 110.67 are unchanged.
ROUND 4 REWORK (policy re-audit revision 3): R3-G1 -> the share's full-year count now follows the base anniversary convention (an anniversary on a day the month lacks falls back to the last day of that month) in rule and compute; on this world (start 2018-06-20, filing 2026-09-15) 8 full years either way, so 565.25 and 110.67 are unchanged.
GATES (round 4 final run, 2026-10-13): EXTENDED OK; TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK; REPLAY OK (closures 30/30, 28/28); SOLVABILITY OK; COMPUTE OK (branches mean 77.00, steps mean 17.00, history_rows_max 15, branches_max 80); GROUNDING OK; TRACEABILITY OK; SCOPE OK.
user_scenario: You are Rosalind Pettigrew, seventy-five, a retired schoolteacher living at 427 Larchmere Drive in Westerville. You are friendly, a little chatty, and you like things explained in plain words. Four of the Ridgeline windows put in back in 2018 have gone foggy between the panes. You filed a warranty claim in September, a technician came out on Saturday, September 26, and looked at them, and since then you received a notice that the claim was approved with a prorated share that you would have to accept before the new glass is ordered. You are calling because you want to go ahead with the replacement glass for the four foggy windows and accept your share today. Only when the agent asks you to identify yourself do you give your phone number, 6145550163, and your email, rosalind.pettigrew74@outlook.com; if another detail is needed you give your ZIP code, 43081, or your date of birth, September 30, 1951. If the agent asks for the registration number on your warranty certificate you read it out: WR-4072519. If asked how many windows are affected you say four. If asked whether you have a CareLine plan you say yes, the CareLine Plus plan, for a couple of years now. You have no idea how the share is worked out and you never suggest an amount; if a figure sounds high or low to you, you still leave the working out to the agent. If the agent explains that something on your warranty account has to be billed or settled before your share can be worked out, you say that is all right and let them take care of it; you never raise any such thing yourself. When the agent tells you that accepting the share is something you must do yourself and hands it to you with the figures they worked out, you accept it with exactly those figures. When the agent confirms your share is recorded and the glass can be ordered, you thank them warmly and end the call without asking for anything else.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.warranty_registration_id: value: the registration id returned by find_warranty_registrations; basis: the docstring asks for 'the identifier of the registration ... as returned by the warranty registration lookup'; uniqueness: the customer holds one registration (WR-4072519).
argument_uniqueness_tracing.warranty_claim_id: value: the id of the seal-failure claim filed 2026-09-15; basis: find_warranty_claims and the visit and decision rows tied to it; the docstring asks for 'the identifier of the warranty claim'; uniqueness: the other claims (screen 2019, hardware 2022) are closed and carry no visit on 2026-09-26 and no proration decision.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.visit_date: value: 2026-09-26; basis: the visit row (part_on_order, 2.2 h) in find_warranty_activities and the rule 'dated with the date of the visit'; uniqueness: it is the only visit on the claim, and it carries a trip entry but no labor entry.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.billable_hours: value: 4.0; basis: the labor rule defines 'the billable labor hours, which are booked on the labor charge to one decimal place' as the method hours raised by the lead-safe allowance and multiplied by the labor crew rate, and the tool asks for 'the billable labor hours of the visit as the warranty labor terms define them'; the visit only measured with parts on order, so its method hours are the labor minimum, which for a claim whose decision approved 4 units is the three-unit minimum 1.5 h (not the 2.2 h on site); plus the glass lead-safe allowance 0.5 h (the installation job carried a lead-safe fee; seal claim) = 2.0; times the two-technician labor crew rate 2.0 (trim-wrap method) = 4.0. uniqueness: the rule's booked figure is the billable labor hours, which start from the method hours and are raised by the allowance and multiplied by the crew rate in the stated order; 1.5 is the method hours only, so every correct agent books 4.0.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: 565.25 = 4.0 billable labor hours x (Limited labor rate 119.00 less the 1100 series senior discount 0.05 = 113.05) x Saturday labor rate 1.25 (2026-09-26 is a Saturday) = 565.25, rounded half up to the cent. The standard method alone would give 2.5 h x 119.00 = 297.50.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.share_amount: 110.67: proration share 0.5 (Limited Warranty, 8 full years from 2018-06-20 to filing 2026-09-15, so five full years have been reached); replacement charge per unit = specialty build 395.00 (Specialty Glass Build) + triple-pane add-on 95.00 (triple pane on all 10 openings) + grilles add-on 30.00 (grilles on all 10, laminated on only 2) = 520.00; gross = 0.5 x 520.00 x 4 = 1040.00; less three-unit volume rate 0.05 = 988.00; less CareLine Plus parts discount 0.15 (plan enrolled 2025-03-03, waiting period over) = 839.80; less visit credit 729.13 (accepted 15 days after the 2026-09-29 decision, within 30: trip 163.88 + labor 565.25 booked at step 13) = 110.67, rounded half up to the cent once.

edges.policy_source: The owner's share of a prorated replacement is fixed only after the records carry a labor charge entry for every technician visit on the claim that the warranty terms bill labor for.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The visit of 2026-09-26 on the seal-failure claim is outside the 1-year labor term (coverage start 2018-06-20), so the terms bill labor for it, but the claim carries only a trip_charge entry and no labor_charge entry.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Step 13 books a labor_charge entry of 565.25 dated 2026-09-26 on the claim; the visit credit then rises from 163.88 to 729.13.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: Single edge: the share's prerequisite sentence pins the labor entry first; no parallel prerequisites.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping step 13 leaves visit_credit at 163.88 (trip only), so the share recomputes to 675.92 instead of 110.67, and the 565.25 labor row is missing.

prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: accept_prorated_glass_share_5fbbc0c6 reads no charge entries and never refuses; it books the share with the figures given, so calling it before the labor entry simply books an unsupported figure.
